labelingRule: A finding is labeled supported when a reader who sees only the field name, the field description and the quote would accept the value for that field without outside knowledge.

Quoted fields (names, descriptions, headlines, numbers, years, places, funding, URLs, roles): the quote must state the value. Rewording, rounding and unit changes are allowed ("183k" supports 183000). A different number, year, place, round or entity is unsupported, and so is a figure for a different quantity (a round size is not total funding, forks are not stars, a copyright year is not a founding year).

Classification fields (industry, company type, business model, sells to businesses, target customer, pricing model): the value is a category the reader assigns. It is supported when the quote makes that category the plain, reasonable reading ("an open source Postgres development platform" supports industry "Developer tools / databases"). It is unsupported when the category needs facts the quote does not give, or when the quote points to a different category.
Deliberately wrong findings are labeled unsupported: values swapped in from another company, wrong numbers, and quotes about something else.

Sources: 'recorded' quotes are copied verbatim from the repo's recordings (tests/fixtures/firecrawl/*.json) or from findings in the AIMock fixtures (fixtures/*.json). 'authored' quotes were written for this set, in the style of a company's own pages, for fields the recordings do not cover (headquarters, founding year, funding, headcount) and for companies from public/sample-data.csv. The label depends only on whether the quote supports the value, not on whether the quote is true of the real company.

fields.companyDescription: A brief description of what the company does
fields.industry: The primary industry the company operates in
fields.employeeCount: The number of employees at the company
fields.yearFounded: The year the company was founded
fields.headquarters: The location of the company headquarters
fields.fundingRaised: Total funding raised by the company
fields.fundingStage: The current funding stage (e.g., Pre-seed, Seed, Series A, Series B, Series C, Series D+, IPO)
fields.companyType: The kind of organization: startup, private company, public company, open-source company, nonprofit, agency or government body
fields.businessModel: How the company makes money, e.g. subscription software, usage-based API, marketplace, advertising, hardware sales
fields.sells_to_businesses: Whether the company sells mainly to other businesses rather than to consumers.
fields.target_customer: The kind of customer the company says it serves.
fields.pricing_model: How the company charges: per seat, per usage, flat subscription, quote only.
fields.product_summary: What the company's main product does, in one sentence.
fields.homepage_headline: The main headline on the company's homepage, as written.
fields.open_source_repo: URL of the company's main public source code repository.
fields.open_roles: Job openings the company currently advertises.
fields.github_stars: Number of stars on the company's main GitHub repository.
fields.is_open_source: Whether the company's core product is open source.
